title: Retention drift detector and legal-hold workflow for request artifacts
creator: Sofia Alvarez
description:
Problem: Customers operating under regional retention laws and internal compliance policies need guarantees that retention settings (for prompts, responses, request logs, and metrics) do not drift after configuration changes or releases. Existing retention configuration is flexible, but lacks active monitoring and remediation that ties into legal-hold workflows used by security/compliance teams.

Goal: Ship an automated Retention Drift Detector service plus a Legal-Hold Manager UI and API that together: detect accidental or malicious retention changes, surface a cryptographically-signed audit trail, and provide safe remediation actions (temporary preservation snapshots, policy rollback, and evidence export) for the four artifact classes: prompts, responses, request logs, and metrics. The feature should be tenant-scoped and respect data residency constraints (region-specific hold/exports).

Out of scope: long-term archival pipelines and third-party eDiscovery connectors (these are follow-ups). For this ticket we will focus on detection, notification, and first-response remediation for on-platform storage and evidence exports to customer-controlled buckets in the correct region.
acceptance_criteria: Drift detector runs continuously and emits an alert when a retention configuration differs from the tenant's active baseline (within 5 minutes of change).
Detected drift includes: field-level diffs (TTL change, per-route override, sampled retention toggles) and identifies affected artifact classes (prompts|responses|request-logs|metrics).

Legal-hold workflow allows a compliance user to: apply a tenant-scoped hold (preserve existing and incoming artifacts), snapshot affected shards to a tenant-managed bucket (region-aware), and lock retention until a release action.
All remediation actions produce an immutable audit entry with actor, timestamp, before/after settings, and a signed export token for evidence bundles.
UI shows an incident timeline, affected routes, estimated preserved volume, and one-click export to an approved region.
API endpoints exist for: listing holds, creating/removing holds, querying drift incidents, and triggering snapshot exports. Endpoints follow Redwood API auth and rate limits.
Automated tests and an end-to-end staging run that simulates TTL regression and confirms snapshot export to an S3-compatible bucket in eu-west-1.
comments: 2026-03-10 Sofia Alvarez: Created ticket after SOC-compliance review. Immediate risk: we observed a misconfigured rollout that shortened request-log TTL by 30 days in a customer's dedicated instance during a metadata refactor. Need fast mitigation and clear audit trails.

2026-03-11 Marcus Lee: Scoping session notes added. Proposed components: (1) drift detector service using config-change webhook + periodic reconciliation, (2) legal-hold API and small UI in Console, (3) snapshot agent to export shards to tenant bucket with region-aware presigned URLs.

2026-03-12 Eng-arch review (Kenji Nakamura): Recommend using compaction-safe snapshots to avoid inconsistent KV-cache state when preserving prompts/responses. Will require a lightweight freeze operation for a shard (estimated 2-4s).

2026-03-13 Security (Aisha Kapoor): Legal-hold must enforce KMS key policy for exports; cannot export to regions where customer has no residency agreement. Added security_review_required flag and KMS checklist to attachments.

2026-03-14 Marcus Lee: Implemented initial drift-rule prototype and webhook consumer. Open PR: github.com/redwood-inference/retention/compare/PR-312. Staging export successful to gs://redwood-staging-eu (proof-of-concept). Next: Console flows and signed audit journaling.
notes: Implementation note: drift detection should combine event-driven detection (config change webhook) with periodic reconciliation of the effective policy per route to catch out-of-band DB edits.
Prioritize tenant-scoped holds over global defaults. Holds must be stored in an append-only ledger and replicated to audit logs within 30s.
For metrics, preservation will use aggregate rollups rather than raw metrics by default; raw metric preservation is opt-in due to volume costs.
Work with runtime team to provide freeze API that quiesces token caches briefly to allow consistent snapshotting of prompts/responses per shard.
